audit.whatIsWrong: The entire content layer swaps Swain's W and E: Nevermove is labelled (W), Vision of Empire (E), and the pull is attributed to Vision of Empire. Per the kit, Nevermove is E (root wave that returns, then pull), Vision of Empire is W (long-range eye, 5500-7500 range, slow + reveal). 'flash-W' kill setups should read flash-E.
audit.why: Riot kit data is authoritative: E text says 'roots enemies it hits. Swain can then choose to pull'; W text is the demon eye.
audit.corrected: All slot labels corrected in edits; pull attributed to Nevermove (E); Vision of Empire (W) framed as the long-range slow/reveal that sets up picks.

audit.why: Field exists to carry real cooldowns; kit gives E 12s rank 1 (10 at max, shorter during R), R 120s.

edits.before: His drain mode — disengage and reset the fight when it starts. Its cooldown is the green light — wait for it.
edits.after: Charged Arcanopulse outreaches his 750-range Death's Hand — every poke is cast from ground his whole kit cannot answer.

edits.before: Q the last-hit from beyond his answer range, W the lateral dodge, and walk — a one-way trade he can only end by leaving the lane.
edits.after: Eye of Destruction's centre slow makes the follow-up Q near-unmissable — layer W on his sidestep and the second hit lands itself.

edits.before: Swain wants to hit you with Nevermove (W) then pull with Vision of Empire, but both are slow, telegraphed skillshots you dodge easily; your Arcanopulse (Q) out-ranges everything he has, so poke him each time he steps to CS and out-trade him flat.
edits.after: Swain wants to root you with Nevermove (E) and pull you into Death's Hand range, but the root is a slow, telegraphed skillshot you dodge easily; your Arcanopulse (Q) out-ranges everything he has, so poke him each time he steps to CS and out-trade him flat.

edits.before: Your poke spikes hard on first item and out-damages his sustain; if he can't land Nevermove (W) to root you, his R healing never gets going, so keep distance and his life total steadily drops.
edits.after: Your poke spikes hard on first item and out-damages his sustain; if he can't land Nevermove (E) to root you, his R healing never gets going, so keep distance and his life total steadily drops.

edits.before: Swain scales into a fight tank, but you burst him from outside his engage range; from 2+ items your rotation chunks him before he can flash-W or pull, and your ult zones his flanks, so avoid getting caught and he can't leverage his teamfight ult.
edits.after: Swain scales into a fight tank, but you burst him from outside his engage range; from 2+ items your rotation chunks him before he can flash-E or pull, and your ult zones his flanks, so avoid getting caught and he can't leverage his teamfight ult.

edits.before: You comfortably out-range Swain: his Nevermove (W) and Vision of Empire (E) are slow, clearly telegraphed skillshots, and your charged Arcanopulse (Q) reaches far beyond them. Stand at max range, last-hit safely, and land Eye of Destruction (W) into Q whenever he walks up to farm. As long as you dodge his root, he has no way to start a fight or heal off you. Poke him down and control the lane from distance.

edits.before: From 3-6 you keep bleeding him with W-into-Q while sidestepping his telegraphed root and pull; his only kill setup is landing Nevermove (W) to chain E and Demonic Ascension (R), which you deny by holding range and kiting with your slow. At 6 his ult is a melee-range drain that does nothing if he can't reach you, so simply stay out and keep poking. Slow-push and ward so his jungler can't set up the flash-root angle. Every trade at range is yours.

edits.before: Swain becomes a durable teamfight threat, but you attack him from outside his engage window; by first item your poke out-damages his sustain, and by two items you chunk him before he can flash-W or land a pull. Use Rite of the Arcane (R) to snipe his flanks and keep objectives locked from range. The one thing that flips a fight is getting caught by a blind root, so respect his engage tools with vision, and you out-range and out-poke him all game.

edits.before: Spending E on chip and then watching the dash you bought it for arrive on schedule — the stun is your only 'no' and everyone knows it.
edits.after: Past river his 850-range Nevermove finally has a lane to land in, and that pull is what turns your poke lead into his 120s Demonic Ascension.

edits.before: - Swain Demonic Ascension: matchup-defining — His drain mode — disengage and reset the fight when it starts. Check it before every step-up. - E Shocking Orb is the lifeline; chip damage never gets it. - The ult answers fights, not waves.
edits.after: - Demonic Ascension is a flat 120s at 650 range — break away when it starts and the drain window dies empty. - Nevermove runs 12s down to 10s, and that pull is what gives his R the range it needs. - Your 13s E is the lifeline; chip never gets it.
